synthNotes:
The 2013 house style guide the first sweep read is SUPERSEDED by the January 2019 revision; state every feature's guide-version explicitly and never present a 2013-only rule as house law. Three of the four angles were never run before this round — say which features rest on the academic angle alone. Feature 11's boxed-text date rests on one hedged blog post seen through two witnesses (DMDavid dates it 1979); feature 8's 'four sentences, under 100 words' is Merwin alone; feature 15's ban is Hines alone; features 12 and 13 are Wikipedia relays of unfetched reviews — flag each. Gygax's own account of his voice (Grognardia) belongs in feature 16. Add a coverage row per angle and the register map (which rules bind a settlement dossier, which the read-aloud/boxed register, which the DM page).

R9 SYNTHESIS (the PLACE round): a new Part 'How official D&D writes a SETTLEMENT' from the four new angles — the slot order of a gazetteer entry, the boxed-text discipline, the digits policy, minor versus major places, the publisher's own settlement tables, the staff's rules in their words — each feature with three or more independent sources where the evidence allows and 'witness skipped by triage' where the r8 critic named skipped sole witnesses (features 29, 31, 33, 34, 36, 38, 39, 41, 42, 46). Reconcile the r8 critic's twelve self-contradictions (bold f9 vs f32; the five 'opens with' rules need a level map; the declared clerk f41/f42 vs f37/f17/f3; no digits f6 vs dated registry facts f39/f41 — years must be addressed; f8 never a page vs f41's 'See Durnan, p. 17'; three minima for a minor place f36/f41/f46; PG vs PG-13; f43 vs f45; f2's protagonist rule; f16 vs f27). Keep the bold-numbered feature form. No quotation over twelve words; the PARTIAL table cites a row only for its supported limb.

extraAngles.prompt: HOW OFFICIAL 5e WRITES A SETTLEMENT — the gazetteer chapters this sweep never reached (0 hits each): Icewind Dale: Rime of the Frostmaiden's Ten-Towns chapter (each town's entry and its slot order — population, government, what is here, notable people, the boxed description); Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus's 'Baldur's Gate Gazetteer'; Curse of Strahd's Vallaki and the Village of Barovia; the Sigil chapter of Planescape: Adventures in the Multiverse; the Sword Coast Adventurer's Guide's city entries. LAWFUL ROUTES ONLY: the publisher's own previews and excerpt pages on dndbeyond.com and wizards.com, D&D Beyond preview articles, published free samples, and reviews or read-throughs that QUOTE the entries — above all Justin Alexander's Remix series on exactly these books (thealexandrian.net is this sweep's top host and is ABSENT on them: the Icewind Dale Remix, the Descent into Avernus Remix, the Curse of Strahd posts), Sly Flourish's prep posts, Power Score's reviews. CLAIMS: the SLOT ORDER of a settlement entry; the boxed-text length and grammatical person; whether population and government are given as digits or in prose; how notable people are named (title, name, epithet); how rumours and hooks are set apart from the record; what a MINOR place gets versus a major one; how the entry opens. One limb per claim, a quote under twelve words, the page or section named.

THE PUBLISHER'S OWN SETTLEMENT DOCTRINE, in its own documents (0 rows so far): the 2014 Dungeon Master's Guide chapter 5 'Adventure Environments' → 'Settlements' — the settlement-size table, the Random Settlements tables (Government, Race Relations, Ruler's Status, Notable Traits, Known For, Current Calamity) and the prose advice on describing a settlement; the 2024 DMG's 'Settlements' pages and its boxed-text paragraph (reached before only through Screen Rant); the SRD 5.1 and 5.2.1 (CC-BY) wherever they carry those tables. Routes: the SRD PDFs and their text mirrors, dndbeyond.com's free DMG excerpt and 'Creating a Settlement' preview pages, reviews quoting the tables, the Wayback captures of wizards.com articles. CLAIMS: the exact slot list the publisher uses to define a settlement; whether the publisher's own worked examples use digits in prose; the tone advice in its own words (under twelve words); what the 2024 text changed from 2014.

THE SRD AS A MEASURED CORPUS FOR PLACE PROSE: the SRD 5.1 and 5.2.1 are lawfully downloadable text (CC-BY-4.0). Find the PLACE-describing passages inside them (adventure-environment text, the sample description text, any read-aloud-shaped passage, the settlement tables' prose) and REPORT measured figures per passage: sentence-length mean and spread, second-person density, digits in prose, em dashes, contractions, tense, sentences per paragraph — with the page or section. The kit already holds a fingerprint of the SRD 5.2.1 RULES pages (pp. 5–18); this angle measures the place-describing text specifically and states where the SRD has none. Each figure is one claim with its measured value and the exact passage; a claim of absence names the pages searched.

THE EDITORIAL STAFF IN THEIR OWN WORDS (zero rows so far): Kim Mohan (the author of the 2021 style-guide docx the section calls current law — interviews, posts, talks on the house style), Michele Carter, Scott Fitzgerald Gray, Christopher Perkins on writing settlements and boxed text, Jeremy Crawford and Chris Sims on the 'D&D voice', the Dragon magazine writers' guidelines of the Mohan and Moore eras, the DMs Guild 'Style Guide' and 'Guide to Publishing' PDFs, the Adventurers League Season 8 content template (the document feature 16's corrective corrects). Routes: podcast show notes and transcripts, ENWorld and Dragon+ archives on Wayback, the DMs Guild PDFs, the Dragon guidelines on Wayback. CLAIMS: what the staff say a settlement entry must carry; the second-person policy in their words; boxed-text length; the no-page-number and term-typography rules as the staff state them; who wrote the style guide and when it moved.
